title: Canonical small-presentation coefficient ring and derived completion
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with $E$ in any universe independently of the scheme $X$. Let $E^s=\operatorname{Shrink} E$ be its canonical small presentation, with field and algebra structures transported along the canonical algebra equivalence $E^s\simeq E$, and spectral norm. Put $\underline{\mathcal O_{E^s}}(S)=C(S,\mathcal O_{E^s})$, using the condensed continuous-ring construction [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_{E^s}}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Form internal modules and their unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Define the positive-level reduction rings $B_{n,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_{E^s}/\pi^{n+1}}$ and their canonical quotient transitions. Derived completeness on this presentation is the condition of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: for a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, the specified augmentation $(c,0):P\to\operatorname{Roos}(P\otimes_{R_X}B_{n,X})$ becomes invertible in the derived category, where $c$ consists of the tensor-unit maps, the Roos differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, and $s$ is induced by the quotient transitions. The canonical derived reduction functors, their transition maps, and normalized towers are formed by derived extension and exact restriction of scalars. A tower is normalized when the transition-induced comparison after extension from level $n+2$ to level $n+1$ is invertible. This is a presentation of the recorded completion notion, not an additional condition on $E$ or $K$.

source.place: canonical reduction comparison and normalized towers, using finite-dimensional smallness in the integral-heart coefficient setting

proof.text: The pulled-back regular module has definitionally the same action as the regular module of the pulled-back ring, giving pullback_regular by reflexivity. For each finite quotient, the quotient map from the integers is an open quotient map; its composite with the consecutive transition is the smaller quotient map. The quotient universal property therefore gives continuous_transition.

The composite of the coefficient reduction with the consecutive quotient transition equals the smaller reduction pointwise on continuous functions. Ring morphisms preserve multiplication, so the reduction and transition maps commute with the integral scalar actions. This proves coefficient_linearity and, after applying inverse image, quotient_transition.

In roosD_sq project to the two biproduct factors. The first coordinate vanishes by d squared equals zero. In the second coordinate expand both subtractions, use that oneSubShift is a chain map and d squared equals zero, and identify the two surviving terms by transport along the degree equality. Their difference is zero.

The quotient units are compatible with consecutive transitions because the reductions factor through the quotients. Tensoring and applying the cochain-complex functor preserves this identity. Product extensionality then gives unitProduct composed with oneSubShift equals zero. Project the augmentation chain-map equation to its two coordinates: the first is the chain-map equation for unitProduct, and the second is the just-proved zero composite. This proves augmentation_comm.

For the derived extension/termwise restriction adjunction [def-sfb-derived-extend-levelwise-adjunction], the hom equivalence sends a morphism f to unit followed by restriction of f (Mathlib Adjunction.homEquiv_unit). By the definition of derivedStep, its inverse image under this equivalence is exactly the component of reductionComp. That component is invertible because reductionComp is a natural isomorphism. Thus every consecutive comparison is invertible, proving derivedReduction_isNormalized.
